library(here)
library(knitr)
source("../prep (May 2025).r")

## Data Loading

The State of Origin reports changed format across years. Three loaders handle the three distinct schemas (FY18–21, FY22–23, FY24–25), then all eight files are harmonised into a single tidy table.

```{r}
#| label: load-data

# FY18–FY21: 7 cols, 1-row title header to skip
load_soo_early <- function(path, year) {
  read_excel(path, skip = 1) |>
    select(
      origin_state  = 1, material_group = 3, material_code = 4,
      material_desc = 5, qty_lbs = 6,        value_usd = 7
    ) |>
    mutate(
      fiscal_year   = year,
      material_code = as.character(material_code),
      qty_lbs       = as.numeric(qty_lbs),
      value_usd     = as.numeric(value_usd)
    )
}

# FY22–FY23: 6 cols, no skip
load_soo_mid <- function(path, year) {
  read_excel(path) |>
    select(
      origin_state  = 1, material_group = 2, material_code = 3,
      material_desc = 4, qty_lbs = 5,        value_usd = 6
    ) |>
    mutate(
      fiscal_year   = year,
      material_code = as.character(material_code),
      qty_lbs       = as.numeric(qty_lbs),
      value_usd     = as.numeric(value_usd)
    )
}

# FY24–FY25: hierarchical format; state rows identified by NA material_code
load_soo_late <- function(path, year) {
  df <- read_excel(path)
  names(df) <- c("state_or_product", "material_code", "qty_lbs", "value_usd")
  df |>
    mutate(
      origin_state = if_else(is.na(material_code), state_or_product, NA_character_)
    ) |>
    fill(origin_state, .direction = "down") |>
    filter(!is.na(material_code)) |>
    mutate(
      material_desc  = state_or_product,
      material_group = NA_character_,
      fiscal_year    = year,
      material_code  = as.character(material_code),
      qty_lbs        = as.numeric(qty_lbs),
      value_usd      = as.numeric(value_usd)
    ) |>
    select(origin_state, material_group, material_code,
           material_desc, qty_lbs, value_usd, fiscal_year)
}

soo_raw <- bind_rows(
  load_soo_early("data/FY18 State of Origin CNP- FINAL.xlsx",                  2018),
  load_soo_early("data/FY19 State of Origin CNP- FINAL.xlsx",                  2019),
  load_soo_early("data/FY20 SOO CNP Only Data_filtered and formatted.xlsx",    2020),
  load_soo_early("data/FY21SOOCNPProgramOnlyData.xls.xlsx",                    2021),
  load_soo_mid(  "data/FY22StateofOrigin-CNP.xlsx",                            2022),
  load_soo_mid(  "data/FY23StateofOrigin-CNP.xlsx",                            2023),
  load_soo_late( "data/FY24StateofOriginReport-CNP.xlsx",                      2024),
  load_soo_late( "data/FY25StateofOriginReport-CNP.xlsx",                      2025)
)

# Remove subtotal / grand total rows
soo <- soo_raw |>
  filter(
    !str_detect(origin_state, regex("total", ignore_case = TRUE)),
    !is.na(material_code)
  )
```

After cleaning, the dataset contains **`r nrow(soo) |> comma()`** purchase records across eight fiscal years.

::: {.callout-note}
FY2024 and FY2025 source files use a condensed format that drops the material group (food category) column. Trend charts that rely on that column are therefore limited to FY2018–FY2023.
:::

---

## Annual Totals

```{r}
#| label: annual-totals
by_year <- soo |>
  group_by(fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(
    total_lbs   = sum(qty_lbs,   na.rm = TRUE),
    total_value = sum(value_usd, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(price_per_lb = total_value / total_lbs)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-lbs-by-year
#| fig-cap: "Total pounds of food purchased through the CNP State of Origin programme, by fiscal year."

ggplot(by_year, aes(x = fiscal_year, y = total_lbs)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2018:2025) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 1e-9, suffix = "B lbs")) +
  labs(
    x = "Fiscal Year",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Total Pounds Purchased"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-value-by-year
#| fig-cap: "Total dollar value of CNP food purchases by fiscal year."

ggplot(by_year, aes(x = fiscal_year, y = total_value)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2018:2025) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(scale = 1e-9, suffix = "B")) +
  labs(
    x = "Fiscal Year",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Total Dollar Value of Purchases"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-price-per-lb
#| fig-cap: "Average cost per pound across all CNP food purchases."

ggplot(by_year, aes(x = fiscal_year, y = price_per_lb)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2018:2025) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_dollar(accuracy = 0.01)) +
  labs(
    x = "Fiscal Year",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Average Price per Pound"
  )
```

## Food Category Trends {#sec-categories}

Material group (food category) is available for FY2018–FY2023 only.

```{r}
#| label: top-categories
# Identify top 10 categories by total pounds purchased (FY18–FY23)
top_groups <- soo |>
  filter(!is.na(material_group)) |>
  group_by(material_group) |>
  summarise(total_lbs = sum(qty_lbs, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(total_lbs, n = 10) |>
  pull(material_group)

by_group_year <- soo |>
  filter(material_group %in% top_groups) |>
  group_by(fiscal_year, material_group) |>
  summarise(
    total_lbs   = sum(qty_lbs,   na.rm = TRUE),
    total_value = sum(value_usd, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-categories-lbs
#| fig-cap: "Annual pounds purchased for the 10 largest food categories (FY2018–FY2023)."
#| fig-height: 6

ggplot(by_group_year, aes(x = fiscal_year, y = total_lbs, colour = material_group)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2018:2023) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M lbs")) +
  labs(
    x      = "Fiscal Year",
    y      = NULL,
    colour = "Food Category",
    title  = "Pounds Purchased by Food Category"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 7)) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 4))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-categories-share
#| fig-cap: "Share of total pounds purchased for each of the top 10 food categories."
#| fig-height: 6

by_group_year |>
  group_by(fiscal_year) |>
  mutate(share = total_lbs / sum(total_lbs)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fiscal_year, y = share, fill = material_group)) +
  geom_area(position = "stack") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2018:2023) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent()) +
  labs(
    x    = "Fiscal Year",
    y    = NULL,
    fill = "Food Category",
    title = "Category Share of Total Pounds (Top 10)"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 7)) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 4))
```

## Animal Protein Share {#sec-animal-protein}

The material group field is absent from FY2024–FY2025 source files, but material codes are consistent across all years. A code-to-group lookup built from FY2018–FY2023 — supplemented with 11 manually assigned codes for new FY2024–FY2025 items — allows the classification to extend across the full period.

```{r}
#| label: build-lookup

# Code → group lookup from years where material_group is present
code_lookup <- soo |>
  filter(!is.na(material_group), !is.na(material_code)) |>
  distinct(material_code, material_group)

# 11 new codes appearing only in FY2024–FY2025, classified manually
manual_lookup <- tribble(
  ~material_code, ~material_group,
  "110151",  "FRUIT, FRESH",
  "111751",  "EGG PRODUCTS",
  "111761",  "CHICKEN, FROZEN",
  "111750",  "YOGURT",
  "111881",  "CHICKEN, COOKED",
  "111790",  "FRUIT, JUICE",
  "111893",  "TURKEY, COOKED",
  "111895",  "FRUIT, FRESH",
  "111900",  "TURKEY, COOKED",
  "111882",  "TURKEY, COOKED",
  "111860",  "BEANS, DRY"
)

full_lookup <- bind_rows(code_lookup, manual_lookup)

# Fill in material_group for FY2024–FY2025 rows using the lookup
soo_full <- soo |>
  left_join(full_lookup |> rename(group_filled = material_group),
            by = "material_code") |>
  mutate(material_group = coalesce(material_group, group_filled)) |>
  select(-group_filled)
```

```{r}
#| label: classify-protein-types

meat_groups <- c(
  "BEEF, CANNED", "BEEF, COOKED", "BEEF, FRESH", "BEEF, GROUND", "BEEF, SPECIAL TRIM",
  "CHICKEN, BULK", "CHICKEN, CANNED", "CHICKEN, COOKED", "CHICKEN, FROZEN",
  "PORK, CANNED", "PORK, COOKED", "PORK, FROZEN",
  "TURKEY, BULK", "TURKEY, COOKED", "TURKEY, FROZEN",
  "HAM, FULLY COOKED", "FISH, CANNED", "FISH, FROZEN"
)
dairy_groups <- c(
  "CHEESE PROC, KOSHER", "CHEESE, MOZZARELLA", "CHEESE, NATURAL AMER", "CHEESE, PROCESSED",
  "MILK, UHT", "YOGURT"
)
egg_groups <- "EGG PRODUCTS"
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-animal-protein-share
#| fig-cap: "Share of total CNP purchase value attributable to each protein type, FY2018–FY2025."

soo_full |>
  filter(!is.na(material_group)) |>
  group_by(fiscal_year) |>
  summarise(
    total     = sum(value_usd, na.rm = TRUE),
    meat_val  = sum(value_usd[material_group %in% meat_groups],  na.rm = TRUE),
    dairy_val = sum(value_usd[material_group %in% dairy_groups], na.rm = TRUE),
    egg_val   = sum(value_usd[material_group %in% egg_groups],   na.rm = TRUE),
    plant_val = total - meat_val - dairy_val - egg_val,
    .groups   = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(meat_val, dairy_val, egg_val, plant_val),
               names_to = "type", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(
    share = value / total,
    type  = factor(type,
                   levels = c("plant_val", "egg_val", "dairy_val", "meat_val"),
                   labels = c("Plant-based", "Eggs", "Dairy", "Meat/Poultry/Fish"))
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fiscal_year, y = share, fill = type)) +
  geom_area(position = "stack") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2018:2025) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(), expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Meat/Poultry/Fish" = "#8B2020",
      "Dairy"             = "#D4956A",
      "Eggs"              = "#F2C96E",
      "Plant-based"       = "#5A8A5A"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x    = "Fiscal Year",
    y    = NULL,
    fill = NULL,
    title = "Share of USDA CNP Purchases by Protein Type",
    subtitle = "Dollar value, FY2018–FY2025"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## Geographic Patterns

```{r}
#| label: top-states
by_state_year <- soo |>
  group_by(fiscal_year, origin_state) |>
  summarise(
    total_lbs   = sum(qty_lbs,   na.rm = TRUE),
    total_value = sum(value_usd, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# States with highest total pounds across all years
top_states <- by_state_year |>
  group_by(origin_state) |>
  summarise(overall_lbs = sum(total_lbs), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(overall_lbs, n = 12) |>
  pull(origin_state)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-top-states-bar
#| fig-cap: "Top 12 states by total pounds supplied to the CNP over FY2018–FY2025."

by_state_year |>
  filter(origin_state %in% top_states) |>
  group_by(origin_state) |>
  summarise(total_lbs = sum(total_lbs), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(origin_state = fct_reorder(origin_state, total_lbs)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = total_lbs, y = origin_state)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 1e-9, suffix = "B lbs")) +
  labs(
    x     = NULL,
    y     = "Origin State",
    title = "Total Pounds Supplied (FY2018–FY2025)"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-top-states-trend
#| fig-cap: "Year-over-year pound volume for the top 12 supplying states."
#| fig-height: 7

by_state_year |>
  filter(origin_state %in% top_states) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fiscal_year, y = total_lbs)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  facet_wrap(~origin_state, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(2018, 2021, 2025)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = "M")) +
  labs(
    x     = "Fiscal Year",
    y     = "Pounds (millions)",
    title = "Annual Purchase Volume — Top 12 States"
  )
```

## Summary Table

```{r}
#| label: tbl-annual-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Annual CNP purchasing summary."

by_year |>
  mutate(
    `Fiscal Year`    = fiscal_year,
    `Total Lbs`      = comma(total_lbs),
    `Total Value`    = dollar(total_value),
    `Avg $/lb`       = dollar(price_per_lb, accuracy = 0.01)
  ) |>
  select(`Fiscal Year`, `Total Lbs`, `Total Value`, `Avg $/lb`) |>
  knitr::kable()
```
